github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGenerat.text: Always generate Git commit messages in English.
Strictly follow the Conventional Commits format: <type>(<scope>): <subject>. If the scope cannot be determined, use <type>: <subject>.
The type must be one of: feat, fix, refactor, docs, test, chore, perf, build, ci, or style.
Use lowercase English for type and scope. Keep the scope short and omit it when no meaningful scope can be determined.
Write a concise subject that describes the purpose of the change and starts with a lowercase imperative verb, such as add, fix, update, remove, refactor, or bump.
Preserve the correct capitalization of proper nouns, product names, and acronyms, such as GitHub, JavaScript, OAuth, API, URL, and HTTP.
Do not list changed filenames or implementation details unless a filename is the actual subject of the change.
For a version-only change, prefer the format chore(release): bump version to <version>.
Output exactly one line. Do not use Markdown or add explanations, a body, or bullet points.
Keep the entire line within 72 characters and do not end it with a period.
